issues.detail: Hebrew 'נֶפֶשׁ קִנְיַן כַּסְפּוֹ' means 'a person bought with his money' (a slave purchased as property), not '買了性命作財物' (bought a life as property). The Chinese rendering '買了性命' (bought a life) misrepresents the object: it is a person/slave, not an abstract 'life'. This changes the meaning from purchasing a slave to purchasing a life.
